{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.4 (TrueLink Agreement)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Client-side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of the TrueLink Interface, Hosting and Support Services Agreement

## Executive summary

We have completed our playbook review of Exhibit 10.4 and marked up the document. The commercial architecture is workable, but the risk allocation is materially one-sided in TrueLink's favour on the three issues we treat as non-negotiable: indemnification, ownership of our data and work product, and limitation of liability.

- **Indemnity (§ 12)** runs essentially one way. TrueLink indemnifies only for its own breach or failure to perform, with no IP-infringement, breach-of-law, data-breach or misconduct cover, while our indemnity in 12(a) is very broad and applies "without regard to any knowledge limitation."
- **Ownership (§ 2)** confirms only TrueLink's rights. The "TrueLink Intellectual Property" definition sweeps in everything "associated with the Interface" — including customisations we pay for — and § 8(d) grants TrueLink a worldwide right to resell and exploit our borrowers' Credit Data.
- **Liability (§ 12)** is capped for TrueLink alone, and only as to §§ 3, 4, 7 and 11. Our exposure, including under the broad 12(a) indemnity, is unlimited, with no floor, no mutual consequential-damages exclusion and no Excluded Claims.
- Secondary but significant: the § 3(i) sole-source obligation to order every credit report from TrueLink with no performance exit; monthly take-or-pay minimums that renew automatically (§§ 5–6); no TrueLink performance warranty beyond Y2K (§ 9); no transition assistance or data return on exit; and no insurance provision at all.
- Several areas already meet our preferred position and require no redline: no audit rights against us, no non-solicitation, no liquidated damages or early-termination fee, an MFN that runs in our favour, and California law/courts with no arbitration.
- One open diligence item: § 8(d) subjects the Credit Data licence to a "Non-Competition Agreement" that is neither defined nor attached. We cannot clear the non-compete question without seeing it.

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Issue / position taken |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. | No TrueLink IP-infringement, breach-of-law, data-breach or misconduct indemnity; our 12(a) indemnity is far broader. We added the standard Vendor limbs and flagged the asymmetry. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 2 LICENSE. | Only TrueLink's ownership is confirmed; § 8(d) permits resale of borrower Credit Data. We added Client ownership of data and Support Services work product, a licence-back of embedded TrueLink IP and a no-joint-ownership statement. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. | One-way cap limited to §§ 3, 4, 7 and 11; our liability unlimited. We made the cap mutual at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000 with standard Excluded Claims. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 2 LICENSE. | § 3(i) requires a TrueLink credit report for every borrower underwritten through the Interface, with no exit. We narrowed it to Interface transactions and added an exit for missed § 3 service levels or failure to supply data. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 2 LICENSE. | Grant covers Client only (§ 8(c) limits access to our officers, employees and agents), is non-transferable, and § 13 terminates it "promptly" with no cure period. We extended it to affiliates and contractors, added successor transfer and limited revocation to termination. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. | No M&A/successor carve-out and consent is unqualified. We added the successor carve-out, a "not unreasonably withheld" standard, a bar on assignment to our competitors, and confirmation that a change of control gives TrueLink no termination or re-pricing right. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. | We have a convenience exit (within fallback), but notice is indeterminate (30–60 days) and prepaid fees are non-refundable. We set 30 days' notice without penalty plus pro-rata refund. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Needs review | § 2 LICENSE. | No restraint in this document (§ 2(a) preserves our freedom to build or buy competing software), but § 8(d) incorporates an undefined, unattached "Non-Competition Agreement." No redline pending review. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. | No liquidated damages, penalty interest or early-termination fee; § 7 anti-spam covenant and § 8(f) enforcement right carry no monetary penalty. No redline. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments | Deviation | § 5 COMPENSATION. | § 5(a) monthly minimums regardless of usage, § 6 removes any right to contest, on an auto-renewing term. We limited minimums to the current 12-month term, made them reducible on 30 days' notice, and confirmed true-up (not penalty) treatment with no post-termination accrual. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty | Deviation | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | Only express warranty is Y2K date handling (§ 9); § 3 is "reasonable commercial efforts" and § 12 disclaims implied warranties. We added workmanlike-performance and 90-day conformance warranties with repair/re-perform/refund, carved out of the disclaimer. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Exit assistance and data return | Missing | § 12 INDEMNITY. | Exit places the whole migration burden on us (30-day name server, 60-day hosting) with no transition assistance, data return or deletion certification, though TrueLink holds the Web Site, borrower data and backups. We inserted the standard paragraph. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. | 12-month renewal and 30-day window are acceptable, but § 6 price protection lapses after year one. We added a 60-day reminder and capped increases at the lesser of CPI and 3%. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. | No audit, inspection or usage-verification right against us; § 9 access is limited to TrueLink's own Y2K repairs. No redline. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | No non-solicit, no-hire or inducement restriction anywhere in the Agreement. No redline. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. | The only MFN runs in our favour (Hosting Services rates may not exceed those charged to any other party). Keep as drafted. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY. | California law, exclusive California state/federal courts, no arbitration — within our fallback. Venue in TrueLink's home county (San Luis Obispo) is a trade item only. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 12 INDEMNITY. | No insurance provision at all, despite TrueLink hosting our web site and processing borrower credit data. We inserted CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M and workers' compensation, certificates on request. |

## Walk-away items

We should not sign without movement on the following:

1. **Vendor indemnity (§ 12).** A third-party IP-infringement indemnity for the Interface and Hosting Services, plus breach-of-law, data-breach and misconduct limbs, and rebalancing of our "without regard to any knowledge limitation" indemnity in 12(a).
2. **Ownership and use of our data (§ 2; § 8(d)).** Express confirmation that we own our borrower/applicant data and the Support Services work product, and removal or tight limitation of TrueLink's worldwide right to resell and exploit our borrowers' Credit Data.
3. **Mutual liability cap with carve-outs (§ 12).** Unlimited Client exposure sitting beneath a one-way, section-specific cap is not acceptable. We need mutuality, agreement-wide application, the USD floor, a mutual consequential-damages exclusion, and carve-outs for confidentiality/data security and indemnification.
4. **Sole-source obligation (§ 3(i)).** A performance-based exit is required; a term-long, auto-renewing requirement to buy every credit report from TrueLink with no service-level remedy is unacceptable alongside the § 5(a) minimums.

## Next steps

1. Send our redline to TrueLink with the four walk-away items identified as gating, and the § 12 cap, indemnity and § 2 ownership language marked as non-negotiable in substance.
2. Request the **Non-Competition Agreement** referenced in § 8(d) before we clear the non-compete rule; we cannot confirm the absence of a restraint on our business until we have reviewed it.
3. Table the secondary deviations as a package trade: § 5(a)/§ 6 minimums and renewal pricing, licence scope for affiliates and contractors, assignment/change-of-control, the 30-day convenience notice with pro-rata refund, the performance warranty, transition assistance and data return, and the insurance section (fallback: E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M).
4. Hold the San Luis Obispo venue point in reserve as a concession we can accept if the § 12 items land.
5. Confirm with the business the expected monthly credit-report volumes so we can size the reducible minimum under § 5(a) before the next exchange."}
